questions.question: Why must large food molecules like carbohydrates, proteins, and fats be digested?
options: To make them taste better
To break them down into smaller molecules that can be absorbed
To convert them directly into water and carbon dioxide
To allow them to pass through the stomach without being changed

questions.question: How are absorbed nutrients transported to the cells where they are needed?
options: By travelling through the nervous system
By dissolving in the water of the lymphatic system only
By being carried in the blood flow around the body
By moving through the digestive tract again

questions.question: By what process do nutrient molecules that are small enough enter the blood from the digestive system?
options: Active transport only
Osmosis of solids
Diffusion
Filtration through pores

questions.question: Which of the following is an adaptation of the small intestine lining that increases the amount of absorption?
options: A very thick muscular wall to squeeze food
A large surface area provided by many tiny villi
A smooth, slippery mucus coating that prevents absorption
A highly acidic environment that kills all bacteria

questions.question: Which statement best describes a single bacterium?
options: A non-living particle made of proteins
A multicellular organism with complex tissues
A microorganism made of a single living cell
A microscopic fungus that reproduces by spores

questions.question: Which of the following statements about bacteria is true?
options: All bacteria are pathogens that cause serious disease.
Many bacteria are harmless and some are even helpful.
No bacteria can survive inside the human body.
Bacteria are only helpful when they are dead.

questions.question: Where in the human body do helpful bacteria live to assist with digestion?
options: Inside the stomach cavity
Inside the human digestive system
On the surface of the tongue
Inside the salivary glands

questions.question: How do helpful bacteria in our digestive system help us digest food that we cannot digest ourselves?
options: They physically chew the food in the gut
They release enzymes that break down the food
They produce acid that dissolves the food
They absorb the food whole and digest it inside their own cells

questions.question: How do helpful gut bacteria protect us against harmful pathogens that enter our digestive system?
options: By producing white blood cells to attack them
By competing against them for resources and space
By building a physical barrier made of calcium
By increasing the temperature of the digestive tract

questions.question: What is a key difference between mechanical and chemical digestion?
options: Mechanical digestion uses enzymes, while chemical digestion uses teeth.
Mechanical digestion physically breaks food into smaller pieces, while chemical digestion uses enzymes to break chemical bonds.
Mechanical digestion only happens in the small intestine, while chemical digestion only happens in the mouth.
Mechanical digestion creates new substances, while chemical digestion does not change the molecules.

questions.question: What role do enzymes play in the chemical digestion of carbohydrates, proteins, and fats?
options: They act as physical grinders to crush the food.
They act as biological catalysts to speed up the process.
They increase the temperature of the stomach to melt the food.
They dissolve the food by making the environment highly alkaline.

questions.question: Enzymes digest proteins into which smaller molecules?
options: Fatty acids
Glycerol
Amino acids
Simple sugars

questions.question: Which chemical reagent is commonly used to test for the presence of the large carbohydrate molecule starch?
options: Biuret reagent
Iodine solution
Ethanol
Benedict's solution

questions.question: Which chemical reagent is used to test for small sugar molecules, such as those produced from the breakdown of starch?
options: Iodine solution
Benedict's reagent
Biuret solution
Ethanol

questions.question: Which of the following lists the major organs of the digestive system in the correct order that food moves through them?
options: Mouth, stomach, oesophagus, small intestine, large intestine
Mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine
Mouth, oesophagus, stomach, large intestine, small intestine
Oesophagus, mouth, stomach, small intestine, large intestine

questions.question: Which organ is adapted to produce acid and enzymes to chemically digest proteins while churning food into a liquid mixture?
options: The mouth
The stomach
The large intestine
The pancreas

questions.question: What happens to food that cannot be digested by the body?
options: It is absorbed into the blood and exhaled by the lungs.
It is converted into urine by the kidneys.
It is passed out of the body as faeces.
It is stored permanently in the liver.
